title: First all-returned time of the counter bank
statement: Let $l,W\in\mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $p$ be a valid input-head position for $x$. For each of the $l$ counters, choose a selection bit $a_i$ and a natural number $n_i$, and suppose the binary expansion of each $n_i$ has length at most $W$. Starting the bank with counter $i$ in carry control when $a_i$ is true and in return control otherwise, with its tape holding the binary expansion of $n_i$ and its head at zero, there is a time $t\le 2W+2$ such that at every earlier time the bank is not in the configuration where every component has return control, and at time $t$ its configuration is exactly the bank configuration with every component in return control, each tape holding the binary expansion of $n_i+1$ if $a_i$ is true and of $n_i$ otherwise, and each head at zero.
hypotheses_covered: binary expansion of each $n_i$ has length at most $W$
replaced: For every input word, input position, selection vector, counter values, and common width bound $W$, there is a time $t \le 2W + 2$ such that the bank control is not all-returned at any earlier time, and at $t$ the bank holds exactly the requested incremented values with every head restored to zero. The duration may be zero when nothing is selected; positivity is supplied by the surrounding dispatch controller.
